**Clean delta (merges after #1622, which merges after #1615).** No blockers found.

**Scope of this review: only what #1634 adds after c74d888d** (`git diff c74d888d..881f7726`: ae1651db, 881f7726; no merge commits in that range). #1615 and #1622 are not re-reviewed here. NeoTech's needs-rework on #1615 still stands, and this PR cannot merge before #1615 and #1622 do.

**What looks good**
- `keep_law::is_hole_kind` is narrow (Drill without cross holes, Bore, Thread); the cross drill is left out and filed as #1635.
- Both `run_job` frame arms carry the same law. The hole kinds now get `Contain` against the setup's parts and are removed from the `Keep` branch, so no part is judged twice. A Chamfer on a stock source goes through the existing `Keep` branch with the parts.
- The wall excuse is only `holes`' own vertical axes (`HoleAxis::vertical`, to the facet sagitta, #1205) plus a thread's declared `bores` (#1071). It is measured about the declared hole's axis, so it cannot excuse a neighbour part's wall elsewhere.
- Part-source Drill/Bore/Thread/Chamfer on a single-part job is unchanged by construction. `parts_in_stock` returns empty for a part-solid source, so `parts_holed` is false. `neighbour_parts` is empty with one part, so the new tap-core branches never run. The related suites below pass unchanged.
- The tap-core re-read fix is real: with it disabled, tests go red (below).
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` in the production diff (only in test helpers). Test files are 162 and 376 lines. Decision file present. Body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1631`.

**Results** (locally, trial-merged with current upstream/main, which does not yet hold #1615/#1622; self-hosted runner status could not be read - 403 on the runners API - so the local path was used)
| check | result |
|---|---|
| `stock_source_holes` (6 pins) | 6 passed |
| Mutation M4: stock-source parts out of the tap-core re-read | red: `a_hole_kind_off_the_stock_into_the_part_gouges_and_never_posts` |
| Mutation M5: neighbours out of the tap-core re-read | red: `a_tap_through_a_neighbouring_part_is_not_acquitted_at_its_core` |
| camcraft-app lib + 26 suites around the touched code (keep_law, stock_source_law/verdict, neighbour_law, drilling_cross*, bore_*, thread_*, tap_sim, drill_prior, edge_break_*, mark_floor, solid_law, hole_wall_*, mill2d_b/c, setup_stock_source, tilt, mcp_verify, coarse_contain, golden_cl) | all ok, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` | clean |
Not run: the full quick gate (the author reports it green), M1-M3, M6, M7.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. The flush-stock Chamfer refusal is a generic `Gouge` on the op. Neither the warning text nor anything the user sees names the workaround (chamfer with the part as the source); it is only in the decision file and PR body. MCP `add_operation` defaults the source to the stock, so an agent that chamfers a part cut to its stock size will meet this with no hint. The false refusal is limited to stock edge on or inside the part, but a one-line hint on the gouge for `Chamfer2D` with a stock source would make it self-explaining. A follow-up (P7) is enough.
2. `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` is 3572 lines (+~25 here). It was already far over 400; flagging growth only.
3. The 3+2 arm and the turned-stock MCP case are not exercised (as the author says), and I did not exercise them either; the 3+2 branch is a mirror of the aligned one by reading.
4. #1635 (cross drill on a stock source) remains open for P1.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 881f7726842a48ebf3d6731556e2ec65dc7505b6 -->
**Review of the two commits after c74d888d (ae1651db, 881f7726): no blocker in this delta. Stacked: it cannot merge before #1615 and #1622.**

Results, on the self-hosted runner: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43565356761 (trial-merged with main 22b8fe7a), conclusion success. Quick gate: sim ok, motion ok, app ok (1205 s), ui ok, 4 steps, 0 failed. Clippy `-p camcraft-app -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -D warnings`: green. Windows-only readings: none in the diff, not run locally.

**Stack.** #1615 (head 4f05e9c0) is `needs-rework`: its open finding, `crates/sim/src/verify/solid.rs:190-195` (a straight rapid up the tool axis that starts where a cutting move ended skips every check), is still carried in the tree this PR sits on; these commits do not touch it. #1622 (c74d888d) is also unmerged. Merge order: #1615, then #1622, then this.

**Drill with cross holes is still not judged.** It is not a hole kind, so on a stock source it has no part law; the author files it as issue 1635 (P1). The closing keyword for issue 1631 is therefore only partly true: it covers Chamfer, Bore, Thread and Drill without cross holes. Please say that in the body or keep 1635 visible to the maintainer.

---

What I checked by reading the code:
- Hole kinds (generate.rs ~3151-3155 aligned, ~3321-3323 turned): `parts_holed` -> contain_into(keep_parts, DepthLaw::Contain, params holes as vertical axes, thread_bores). Both frame arms apply the same law (the turned arm on `keep_local`, plane frame; bores and holes already used in that frame by the part-source call at 3313). The generic Keep branch is correctly switched off for them (`!parts_holed` in both arms), so no double law and no law dropped.
- What is excused: only facets of a round wall about a declared hole axis (hole_walls, solid.rs:44-53, #1205 sagitta) plus a thread's declared bore. Off-axis, wider, deeper, or where the part models none is a Gouge, as the body says. Residual to try on the run/tests: the excuse is keyed to the declared hole xy, not to the part having a hole there; a part facet that happens to be a round wall about a declared axis is the only thing excused, so this looks sound. The pins use a 32-gon hole and a tool at size, which does go through the excuse. Not exercised: a drill whose axis is correct but whose part hole is much narrower and tessellated coarsely (sagitta excuse margin); a through hole in a part whose hole wall is not axis-aligned.
- Drill WITH cross holes: not a hole kind (is_hole_kind needs `cross.is_empty()`), not in is_stock_kept_kind -> no part law at all on a stock source, so a cross drill into a part in the stock still has 0 op findings (aligned: sim may hold; turned: may post). The author names it as follow-up #1635 (P1). Consequence: issue 1631 titled "Drill" and the closing keyword is only partly true; the P1 gap remains open under 1635. Ask that the PR body say it covers Drill without cross holes only and that 1635 is not forgotten; a maintainer call whether the keyword is acceptable.
- 2D Chamfer: solid Keep law against the parts, nothing excused (generate.rs ~3147-3149, ~3317-3319). A chamfer off a stock flush with the part is now refused on the op (5 gouges), though it posted before; the body states this and the workaround (chamfer with the part as the source). That is a usable operation refused: a P3-class wrong-refusal, accepted by the author on safety grounds. The decision file records it; the op's refusal text is the generic Gouge, it does not say "use the part as source". Suggest (non-blocking) a note to that effect.
- Tap core re-read (generate.rs ~3183-3191): the closure now also reads keep_parts (Contain) and neighbour_parts (Keep) at the core. acquit drops only gouges the core run did not raise, so adding laws to the core run can only keep more gouges, never acquit one: it cannot newly acquit. It convicts newly only what the core itself hits in those parts: a tap in a modelled hole at tap-drill size passes by the wall excuse (note the core re-read passes `&[]` bores, fine for a tap). A part-source tap through a neighbour lid that models no hole is convicted, as the body says. The neighbour law is Keep with no wall excuse: a legal tap through a neighbour's modelled hole is judged by the same plain Keep law already used for the full tap at ~3165, so no new refusal, consistent with #1621.

Tests (read, not watched failing on the old code; they pass in the run): 6 pins in crates/app/tests/stock_source_holes.rs; against the old logic (is_stock_kept_kind without the four kinds, parts_in_stock returns empty) the into-part, chamfer and MCP pins assert gouges > 0 and would fail; the legal-hole pin passes on old code by construction (0 findings) so it guards only against over-refusal. The author lists 7 mutations each shown red; I did not re-run them. The `.expect()`/`unwrap` hits in the diff are all under crates/app/tests/ (test code). No golden or snapshot changed.

Laws: no unwrap/expect/panic in src. Sizes: generate.rs 3572 lines (+~25, already far over; not blocking), keep_law.rs 171, new support mod 376 and test 162. Decision file docs/decisions/1631-stock-holes-chamfer.md present. Body complete (Changelog, closing line, not exercised; the 3+2 arm, MCP on turned stock and cross drill not exercised). No process files touched. Gate map names app::operation::keep_law etc.; tests import app code (placement fine).

Verdict on this delta: clean (not built-red, no requested change beyond the notes above); not ready to merge until its parents are.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
